newsitem.title: UK: British bookmakers stop bets after budget leak.
newsitem.headline: British bookmakers stop bets after budget leak.

text.p: British bookmakers William Hill refused to take bets on the details of Britain's budget on Tuesday after some of the government's annual spending plans were leaked to a British tabloid newspaper.
"We closed the books on the budget after news of the leak. Obviously someone out there knows the details so we couldn't take the risk," said William Hill spokesman Graham Sharpe.
Prime Minister John Major's office confirmed on Tuesday that 36 budget documents that found their way to the editor of the Daily Mirror newspaper on Monday were genuine.
The newspaper called the leak "the shambles of the decade", but did not print the documents, saying publication would have brought chaos to international financial markets.
Sharpe said the bookmakers was still taking bets on the length of British finance minister Kenneth Clarke's budget speech, which started just after 1530 GMT.
"The latest hot tip is it will last 81 to 85 minutes," Sharpe said.

The most popular bet, at 3-1, however, was that the speech would last between 71 and 75 minutes, Sharpe said. For a wager of one pound ($1.67) a correct guess would yield the winner three pounds. ($1=.5990 Pound)
